cards.front: What should you know about plane of movement?
cards.back: An imaginary flat surface that divides the body into sections. Movement occurs ALONG or PARALLEL to a plane.

cards.front: What should you know about axis of movement?
cards.back: An imaginary line around which the body or body part rotates. The axis is always PERPENDICULAR (at 90°) to the plane of movement.

cards.front: What should you know about sagittal plane?
cards.back: Divides the body into left and right halves. Movement in this plane involves flexion and extension - forward and backward movements.

cards.front: What should you know about transverse axis?
cards.back: Runs from left to right through the body. The body or body parts rotate around this axis when performing flexion and extension movements.

cards.front: What should you know about frontal plane?
cards.back: Divides the body into front and back (anterior and posterior) halves. Movement in this plane involves abduction and adduction - side-to-side movements away from and towards the midline.

cards.front: What should you know about sagittal axis?
cards.back: Runs from front to back (anterior to posterior) through the body. The body or body parts rotate around this axis when performing abduction, adduction and lateral movements.

cards.front: What should you know about transverse plane?
cards.back: Divides the body into top and bottom (superior and inferior) halves. Movement in this plane involves rotation - twisting or spinning movements.

cards.front: What should you know about longitudinal axis?
cards.back: Runs from top to bottom (superior to inferior) through the body - from the head down through the spine. The body or body parts rotate around this axis when performing twisting or spinning movements.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — planes and axes of movement?
cards.back: 1. For Planes and Axes of Movement questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Planes and Axes of Movement to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question
